champion: ELANE-associated severe congenital neutropenia with hepatic involvement
ordered_diagnoses: ELANE-associated severe congenital neutropenia with hepatic involvement

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent fever with abdominal involvement and liver pathology
salient_findings: Liver palpable 4 cm below rib margin with tenderness on percussion
Abnormal liver imaging with patchy low-density shadow and honeycomb enhancement
key_facts: Developed fever one week after receiving measles vaccine
Fever initially resolved with Cefuroxime Axetil Granules
Past medical history includes pneumonia, duodenal bulb ulcer, erosive gastritis, and Staphylococcus aureus septicemia and infective endocarditis
Heterozygous mutation in exon 3 of the ELANE gene
Liver tissue showed scattered hepatic structures with focal abscess changes
Culture from liver lesion: Positive for Staphylococcus aureus

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous mutation in exon 3 of the ELANE gene, recurrent fevers, and laboratory findings such as rare neutrophils on the blood film, along with liver involvement as indicated by imaging and pathology results, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Severe Congenital Neutropenia
rejected.why: While the patient has neutropenia, the specific ELANE gene mutation and hepatic involvement point more specifically to ELANE-associated severe congenital neutropenia with hepatic involvement.

rejected.label: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
rejected.why: Although the patient has a liver abscess, this diagnosis does not explain the broader clinical picture of recurrent fevers, neutropenia, and the genetic mutation.

rejected.label: Cyclic Neutropenia
rejected.why: Cyclic neutropenia is characterized by periodic episodes of neutropenia, but the patient's presentation and the genetic findings are more consistent with a congenital form of neutropenia associated with the ELANE gene mutation.

rejected.label: Chronic Granulomatous Disease
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by recurrent infections due to impaired neutrophil function, but the genetic mutation and specific pattern of neutropenia and liver involvement in this case do not align with Chronic Granulomatous Disease.

gold: Severe congenital neutropenia (SCN) with hepatic abscess caused by Staphylococcus aureus
